concepts.statement_en: Module 1 maps to the TESDA BHS NC II competency 'Participate in workplace communication', whose outcomes are: obtain and convey relevant workplace information, perform duties following workplace instructions, and complete relevant work-related documents.
concepts.source: deck slide 6; facilitator-guide PDF 19 (competency table), PDF 20

concepts.statement_en: Asked to name their tasks, BHWs answer in terms of health service delivery; the UHC Act's direction is primary care and health promotion, so the role is wider than service delivery alone.
Under UHC the BHW's roles as community organizer and health educator are emphasised, not only their service-delivery role.
Under the UHC Act, BHWs are designated barangay-level Health Education and Promotion Officers (HEPOs); the three roles described in the DOH BHW Reference Manual sit under that designation.
concepts.source: deck slide 9; reference-manual PDF 11; facilitator-guide PDF 5

concepts.statement_en: Each BHW needs sufficient knowledge of the priority health programmes and health problems in order to share them with their barangay.
Health Educator: gives people the knowledge to keep their bodies and their environment healthy.
The Health Educator keeps teaching people about their health and prepares them for illnesses, accidents and risk factors at each stage of life.
The Health Educator reaches every sector of the community — children through to the elderly — with information, knowledge and training.
Community Organizer: maintains good relationships and communication with community leaders and members, and with city/municipal health staff.
The Community Organizer organises community members and encourages their participation in health activities and advocacy.
The BHW is a member of the barangay planning team for health, helping community leaders understand and act on the barangay's own health problems.
Under UHC, each city's or province's Local Investment Plan for Health (LIPH) recognises the barangay's contribution to health planning, and BHWs are expected to participate in that planning.
Health Service Provider: part of the city/municipal primary care team, assisting the barangay midwife in delivering health services.
BHWs are the community's first contact and frontline health workers when a health service is needed.
The Health Service Provider guides people on where to go to meet their health needs.
BHWs deliver simple initial services themselves: interviewing, taking vital signs, recording, making the household profile, and first aid.
BHWs continue care for their community by monitoring people's health over time.
BHWs help collect and safeguard data and records from the households in their assigned area, and these data guide health programmes.

The BHW's documentation duties: household profiles, master lists of the different groups in the community, registries of people given services, and other government/DOH/LGU forms assigned by the nurse, midwife or doctor.
concepts.source: deck slide 13; reference-manual PDF 12; facilitator-guide PDF 20 (TESDA outcome 'complete relevant work-related documents')

concepts.statement_en: The skills each role needs are taught elsewhere in the curriculum: health-promotion skills under Core Competencies, community-organising skills under Community Mobilization in Common Competencies.
